title: Private Link, private endpoints and service endpoints

videos.script: The shop's storage account has an address on the internet. Anyone who knows its name can knock on that door. {{public}} Your application sits in a private subnet. It still reaches the account the way a laptop in a café does. {{cafe}} There are two other roads. A service endpoint is a switch on a subnet. Traffic from there carries the subnet's identity, and the account's firewall can let the subnet in. {{endpoint}} But the account keeps its public door, and the road leads to every storage account in the region. {{every}} A private endpoint is different. It is a network interface in your own subnet, with a private address. {{nic}} That address is one account, and one service of it. The public door can then be closed for good. {{closed}} The application keeps the same name. What changes is the answer the name gets. {{dns}} Asked from inside the network, it gets the private address. Asked from anywhere else, it gets the public one. {{split}} Most broken private endpoints are broken there, in the DNS. By the end, you will know where to look. {{end}}
